en: The Dhāraṇī of the Auspicious Vasudhārā. Om, homage! To the teaching of the glorious Jina, which brings about the day that destroys the wretchedness of the two types of cyclic existence.
O Vasudhārā, O Sudhādhārā, homage to you; we pray to you with compassion. // 1 //
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was staying in the great city of Kauśāmbī, in the excellent great forest called Kaṇṭaka, in the Ghosita Monastery,

together with a great community of monks numbering about five hundred, and surrounded by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who were rich in asceticism, abundant in self-restraint, and endowed with all the qualities of pure dharmas.
Placing [the Buddha] at his head, he taught the Dharma.
Now at that time, in the great city of Kauśāmbī, there lived a householder named Sucandra.

His senses were tranquil and his mind was serene; he supported many, had many sons and daughters, and was endowed with a large retinue of servants and attendants. He was faithful, a great believer, and possessed of virtuous intentions. He approached the place where the Blessed One was staying.
Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, he circumambulated the Blessed One many hundreds of thousands of times and sat down to one side.
Seated to one side, the householder Sucandra, having found the opportunity, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"I would like to ask the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, about a certain matter, if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to receive an answer to my question."
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the householder Sucandra:
"Ask, householder, whatever you desire; I shall gladden your mind by answering each question as it is asked."
When this had been said, the householder Sucandra, having replied to the Blessed One, "Excellent, Blessed One," and having assented to the Blessed One, addressed him as follows:
"Blessed One, how does a son of good family or a daughter of good family, having been poor, become no longer poor; and having been ill, become no longer ill?
Then the Blessed One, though already knowing [the answer], spoke thus to the householder Sucandra:
"Why do you, householder, ask about poverty? When this was said, the householder spoke thus to the Blessed One:
"I am poor, Blessed One; I am poor, Sugata. I have many dependents, many sons, many daughters, and I am endowed with many servants and attendants.
May the Blessed One show me such a Dharma discourse by which impoverished beings may become free from poverty."
May beings who are diseased become free from disease; may they be endowed with abundant wealth, grain, treasuries, and granaries;

may they be dear, pleasing, charming, and beautiful to behold; may they be lords of giving and great lords of giving, possessing inexhaustible stores of gold, bullion, wealth, grain, jewels, treasuries, and granaries;
and may they be richly supplied with gems, pearls, lapis lazuli, diamonds, conch shells, crystals, coral, gold, and silver.
"And may they possess well-established, prosperous houses, sons, wives, and households.
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the householder Sucandra:
"Householder, in those very incalculable eons that have passed, at a time and in an age long ago, there was a Blessed One, a Tathāgata named Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa."

"Householder, from the presence of that Tathāgata— the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, born in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, knower of the worlds, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One— I heard this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā, and having heard it, I have mastered it."

"It has been upheld, recited, mastered, promulgated, proclaimed, rejoiced in, and extensively revealed to others; O householder, I too shall now speak that *dhāraṇī*, by the power of which *dhāraṇī* human beings do not harass the son of good family, nor do non-humans... *yakṣas*... *rākṣasas*... *pretas*..."
Piśācas, bhūtas, kumbhāṇḍas, skandas, apasmāras, ustras, pūtanās, kaṭapūtanās, and yātudhānas do not cause them harm.
[Nor do] those who feed on urine, blood, excrement, fat, flesh, phlegm, pus, or snot.

Those who feed on phlegm, those who feed on intelligence, those who feed on intoxicants, those who feed on birth, those who feed on life, those who feed on strength, those who feed on garlands, and even those who feed on leftovers do not cause harm to that faithful son of good family or daughter of good family for whom this Dhāraṇī has entered their heart,
come into their hands, reached their ears, been mastered, set in motion, proclaimed, reflected upon, retained, or recited.

It will be written down, approved, and revealed to others; for that son of noble family or daughter of noble family, it will lead to long-term benefit, happiness, welfare, security, abundance, and the accumulation of the requisites for yoga.
And whoever [recites] this great *Vasudhārā-dhāriṇī* for the sake of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones—

Having performed a magnificent worship and paid homage, one should make offerings four times during the night; then those deities, with uplifted minds, joyful, delighted, and full of gladness, will come in person and cause a rain of wealth, grain, silver, gold, and jewels to fall. Being thus pleased—pleased with the teaching of the Tathāgata, pleased by the Buddha’s ordinance, and pleased by the ordinance of the Saṅgha—they shall do so.
I am pleased by the intention of my Dharma-preacher.
Homage to the Triple Gem!
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa.

Namely: Oṃ śrī surūpe suvadane bhadre subhadre bhadravati maṅgale sumāṅgale maṅgalavati argale argalavati candre candravati ale acale acapale udghātini udbhedini ucchedini udyotini śasyavati dhanavati dhānyavati udyotavati śrīmati prabhavati amale vimale.

O stainless one, O Ruru, O beautiful one, O beautiful and pure one, O you who are worthy of worship, O you who are without end, O you who are without limit, O you who are without measure, O you whose hands are bowed low, O mistress of the universe, O night of the universe, O ray of the universe, O you of universal form, O you with nails that are the universe, O you whose head is the universe, O you of pure conduct, O you who are to be concealed, O you who are to be purified, O supreme one, O unsurpassed one, O sprout, O Naṅkura, O illuminator, O Rarame, O Ririme.

Rurume khakhame khikhime khukhume dhadhame dhidhime dhudhume tatare tatare ture ture tara tara tāraya tāraya māṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca vajre vajre vajragarbhe vajropame vajriṇi vajravati ukke bukke nukke dhukke kakke hakke ḍhakke ṭakke varakke āvarttini nivarttini.
O showerer, O great showerer, O increaser, O great increaser, O producer! Recollect, recollect the Tathāgata Vajradharasāgaranirghoṣa;

recollect the truth of all Tathāgatas; recollect the truth of the Saṅgha! O irresistible one, O irresistible one! Heat, heat! Strike, strike! Fill, fill! Fulfill, fulfill for me and my retinue, O Blessed One Vasudhārā!
Support, support, support all sentient beings!
O Śāntamati, Jayamati, Mahāmati, Sumaṅgalamati, Piṅgalamati, Subhadramati, Śubhamati, Candramati: come, come! Remember the pledge! Svāhā!
Remember your own nature! Svāhā!

Dhṛti... the discipline of all Tathāgatas... the heart-mantra... the near-heart-mantra... victory... complete victory... remember the victory over all sentient beings, svāhā! Om śrīṃ vasumukhīṃ svāhā!
Oṃ śrīṃ vasuśrī svāhā / Oṃ śrīṃ vasuśriye svāhā / Oṃ vasumati svāhā /
Oṃ vasumatiśriye svāhā / Oṃ vasve svāhā / Oṃ vasude svāhā /
Oṃ vasuṃdhari svāhā / Oṃ dhariṇi dhāriṇi svāhā / Oṃ samayasaumye samayaṃkari mahāsamaye svāhā /
Oṃ śriye svāhā / Oṃ śrīkari svāhā / Oṃ dhanakari svāhā /
Oṃ dhānyakari svāhā / Root mantra. Oṃ śriye śrīkari svāhā /
Oṃ dhanakari dhānyakari ratnavarṣaṇi svāhā / [This is] the mantra to be accomplished (sādhyamantra).
Oṃ vasudhāre svāhā /
The heart: *lakṣmyai svāhā*.
Om, the near-heart.
Oṃ lakṣmī, to her who dwells upon the earth, svāhā!
Just as [it was said], Oṃ, to her who brings forth the vessel of transport, svāhā!

Do not go far away; you who bring about the production of goods not yet produced, and who cause the increase of goods already produced—truṭe liṭe liṭe li! Come, come hither, O Blessed One! Do not delay!
Fulfill my heart’s desire!

Just as streams of water from the ten directions completely fill the earth, just as the sun dispels long-standing darkness with its rays, just as the moon brings forth medicinal herbs with its cool beams, and just as Indra, Vaivasvata, Varuṇa, and Dhanada [fulfill their purposes].
They always contemplate for men that accomplishment which follows the mind.
Likewise, may these things that I have constantly contemplated according to my desire,
as well as all the mantra-words, be successfully accomplished through effort.

Namely: *suṭa suṭa khaṭa khaṭa khiṭi khiṭi khuṭu khuṭu maru maru muñca muñca maruñca maruñca tarppiṇi tarppiṇi tarjani tarjani dehi dehi dāpaya dāpaya uttiṣṭa uttiṣṭa hiraṇyasuvarṇaṃ pradāpaya svāhā*.
Svāhā to food and drink! Svāhā to the falling of wealth! Svāhā to the cow! Svāhā to Surabhi!
To Vasu, svāhā! To the Lord of Vasus, svāhā! To Indra, svāhā!
Svāhā to Yama! Svāhā to Varuṇa! Svāhā to Vaiśravaṇa!
Svāhā to the cardinal directions and the intermediate directions!
May these mantra-words of mine grant me freedom from doubt and may they rejoice in this!
Om hraṃ hrīṃ, come, come, O Blessed One; give, cause to be given, svāhā!
This is the heart-mantra (*hṛdaya*) of the Blessed Noble Vasudhārā; it is effective even for one who has committed great sins.
It bestows human-sized riches and fulfills one's desired wishes. Like a wish-fulfilling cow, it completely fulfills whatever desires one may long for.
This is the root-vidyā.
Homage to the Triple Gem!
Homage to the Goddess, daughter of the Giver of Wealth, Vasudhārā! Cause the stream of wealth to fall; act, act! O Mistress of Wealth, giver of wealth, O jewel-giver!
O great treasure-trove of gold, wealth, and jewels, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of treasures! Come, come, Blessed One!
Having entered my city, cause a stream of great wealth and grain to fall in my palace; perform, perform! Oṃ hraṃ traṭa, svāhā to the dweller of Kailāsa!
Great Vidyā!
Oṃ Vasudhārā, you who cause the great rain to fall, bestow wealth, svāhā!
The root-heart mantra: Oṃ vasudhāre sarvārthasādhinī sādhaya 2 uddhara 2 rakṣa 2 / sarvārthanidhayantraṃ vava ṭata vava ṭaṇṭa ḍaṇḍa svāhā /

The Supreme Heart Mantra: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Levaḍikā! O you who protect living beings, who hold a fruit in your hand, of divine form, giver of wealth, granter of boons, pure, utterly pure, maker of auspiciousness, maker of peace, destroyer of fear, defiler of fear—shatter all the wicked!

2 Mohaya 2 Jambhaya 2 Stambhaya 2! Grant me peace, prosperity, subjugation, and protection, svāhā! This is the *dhāraṇī* of Levaḍikā. Householder, these are the mantra-words of the *Vasudhārā-dhāraṇī*, belonging to all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
Having performed worship, one should not cease for six months; then it becomes perfected. Furthermore, whichever direction this Great Vidyā is recited in, that direction becomes worthy of worship.
For the purpose of nourishing rites (*pauṣṭika*), whether in one’s own house or another’s house, [one should worship] the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Noble Avalokiteśvara.

And having paid homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the presence of the mantra-deity, one should prepare a square maṇḍala with sandalwood in an auspicious place, such as a treasury or a storehouse, while reciting [the mantra] three times; then, O Householder,
the house of a son of good family or a daughter of good family will be filled with a great abundance of wealth, grain, silver, gold, and jewels.
It destroys all deficiencies and all calamities with every kind of provision.

Therefore, householder, you should take up this *dhāraṇī* named Vasudhārā; uphold it, recite it, teach it, master it, learn it thoroughly, set it in motion, rejoice in it, and reveal it extensively to others.
"It will be for a long night for their benefit, welfare, abundance, security, and the accumulation of the requisites for yoga.

"Excellent, Blessed One! the householder Sucandra replied. Having heard this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā from the presence of the Blessed One, he was thrilled, satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness; he prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One.
Having joined his palms in reverence, he addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One,
this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā has been grasped by me— it has been proclaimed, maintained, recited, mastered, rejoiced in, and reflected upon with the mind—
and it shall now be revealed in detail to others."
Then, at that very moment, the householder named Sucandra became one whose treasuries and granaries were completely full.
Thereupon, the householder Sucandra circumambulated the Blessed One many hundreds of thousands of times,
bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and, looking back at the Blessed One again and again many times, [departed from] the Blessed One.
Having departed from his presence,
the Blessed One then addressed the venerable Ānanda:

"Go, Ānanda, to the house of the householder Sucandra, and see whether his great treasuries and granaries are filled with all kinds of wealth, grain, silver, jewels, gold, and all necessary provisions."
And they were completely full.
Then, having received the Blessed One’s command, the Venerable Ānanda went toward the great city of Kośāmbī, to the house of the householder Sucandra.
Having arrived and entered inside, he saw that it was filled with all kinds of wealth, grain, silver, gold, and all manner of utensils.

Seeing that the great treasuries and storehouses were completely full, he was struck with wonder; filled with joy, contentment, elation, gladness, and rapture, a sense of pleasure and mental well-being arose within him.
He approached the Blessed One, and having arrived, he bowed his head at the Blessed One’s feet and addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, by which the householder Sucandra has become so immensely wealthy, possessed of great enjoyments, with vast treasuries and granaries, and enriched with all kinds of riches and grain?
The Blessed One said:
"Ānanda, the householder Sucandra is faithful; he is supremely faithful and possesses a virtuous intention."
This dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā has been taken up by him; it has been maintained, recited, taught, mastered, fully acquired, proclaimed, and rejoiced in. Now he will also reveal it to others.

Therefore, Ānanda, you too should take up this dhāraṇī named Vasudhārā; maintain it, recite it, teach it, master it, fully acquire it, set it in motion, proclaim it, rejoice in it, and reveal it extensively to others.

For that son of good family or daughter of good family in whose hands, home, or possession this [sūtra] shall come to be as a book, there shall be no occurrence of disease, famine, pestilence, or wilderness perils; his wealth shall gradually increase.
That will be for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, and for the sake of the great mass of beings.
For the happiness of both gods and humans,
Ānanda, I do not perceive any phenomenon— in this world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins,
its gods, humans, and asuras— that can cause this great vidyā-mantra called Vasudhārā to be otherwise.
It is impossible that he would transgress [this];

for what reason? Ānanda, these mantras of the Vasudhārādhāriṇī are indeed indestructible; they will not even reach the path of hearing for those beings whose roots of merit are exhausted, let alone enter into a book.
Having made it, they will keep it in their homes.
For what reason?

For this is the word of all the Tathāgatas; this dhāraṇī has been spoken by all the Tathāgatas, empowered, sealed with their own seal, manifested, revealed, proclaimed, rejoiced in, praised, brought about,
disclosed, made clear, announced, well-expounded, and well-taught for the sake of all beings who are impoverished and afflicted by various diseases.
"And for the sake of warding off all fears and calamities caused by the wicked.
Ānanda said: "I have grasped it, Blessed One; this *dhāraṇī* named Vasudhārā has been retained, recited, mastered, taught, set in motion, proclaimed, rejoiced in, and well-pondered by my mind.
Then the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, and placed his right knee on the ground.
Having established himself upon the earth, he bowed with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was; at that moment, with hands folded together, he uttered this exclamation:
"Inconceivable is the Blessed Buddha, and the Buddha-dharma is also inconceivable."
For here, the existence of beings is inconceivable, and their maturation is also inconceivable.
Lead us to the teaching, O Omniscient One, who has gone beyond old age and death;
O King of Dharma, who has attained the fruit, Heroic Buddha, homage be to you!
Then the venerable Ānanda, thrilled, satisfied, elated, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness, said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, what is the name of this Dharma-discourse, and how shall I remember it?
The Blessed One said:

"Therefore, Ānanda, you should remember this as 'The Inquiry of the Householder Sucandra,' remember it as 'All Wealth and Grain,' and remember it as 'The Ritual Manual of the Vidyārājñī Vasudhārā, Praised by All Tathāgatas. The Blessed One having spoken thus, the venerable Ānanda, those monks, those bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly— including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas— were uplifted and rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
They rejoiced in what was spoken.
Thus ends the Noble Vasudhārādhāriṇī.
Six.
Six.
Six.
In the year 1695, on the 7th day of the dark fortnight of the month of Āśvina, on a Friday.
Six.
Six.
Six.
May this work of Sāhaśrī Pamanīyāsuta, composed by Sāhaśrī Indrajī for the purpose of study and for the benefit of others, be auspicious.
May there be auspiciousness for the scribe and the reader. Śrī.
